bottom_line: Wait. Premarket the chip ETF is down more than 2% and Nasdaq-100 futures about 0.7%, extending the sell-off on data-centre policy fears, which is the worldview's top bearish thesis. Most names are already below their rated price, and two (ONTO, NRG) report on 9 Nov.
what_changed: Nasdaq-100 futures were about -0.7% and S&P futures about -0.1% early Thursday; a chip ETF fell more than 2% premarket on fears of tighter data-centre rules (touches the political-risk thesis, 58).
Oil fell more than 8% on Wednesday to the lowest since 31 Aug, which helped broad stocks but not AI suppliers.
AMD (reported 3 Nov) beat and guided Q4 to about $17bn versus $16.2bn expected, but the stock failed to hold gains as Nvidia and Intel fell: good prints are not lifting prices (demand thesis, 60).
No new after-hours results dated 5 Nov were found.

trust: No ratings are graded yet (grading starts after 28 days). The 33 picks average -6.3% versus QQQ, and Buy/Overweight picks at -5.7% do not beat any baseline except the random pick; only QQQ and SMH are ahead.
if_buying: Overweight means a small starter position, not a full one; add only if the thesis holds.
Wait on NRG, STX, DELL and VRT: their ratings are 2-6 days old and prices have moved against them.
ONTO and NRG report on 9 Nov; avoid holding a new position into that without sizing for a gap.
Use limit orders; the open is likely to be volatile after a 2%+ premarket chip drop.
